title: Wrapper Classes

lines.explanation:
this line imports the ArrayList class from java.util 
package.

This example shows how to store sequence of 
numbers in the ArrayList. To store sequences 
of numbers in an array list, you must turn 
them into objects by using 
wrapper classes. There are wrapper classes 
for all eight primitive types. The 
wrapper 
class names start with uppercase letters, and 
that two of them differ from the 
names of the corresponding primitive type: 
Integer and Character. Each wrapper class 
object contains a value of the 
corresponding primitive type.

Declares an ArrayList AL to store Integer 
objects.

Here, an object of the class Integer that 
contains a value of type int is created and 
added to the list.

Conversion between primitive types and the 
corresponding wrapper classes is automatic. 
This process is called 'auto-boxing'. 
Here, 2 is automatically converted to the 
wrapper class Integer that contains 2 
and then the reference of the wrapper class is 
added to the list.

Wrapper objects are also automatically 
unboxed to primitive types. This conversion is 
called 'unboxing'.
